headline: A weak US jobs report and a chip rally led by Nvidia and Micron pushed the Nasdaq to a record on Friday.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a market recap with hard numbers, no single new event.
importance_line: Slower hiring is bad news for job seekers but eased fears of another Fed rate rise, and AI chip makers again did the lifting for the whole market, which leaves stock prices leaning on a narrow group of companies.
summary: Stocktwits reports that US stocks closed the week higher on Friday after September payrolls grew by only 29,000 against a forecast of 84,000 and unemployment rose to 4.2 percent, cutting the market-implied odds of an October Fed rate rise to 22 percent from 64 percent a week earlier. Semiconductor shares rose about 2 percent on gains in Nvidia, Micron and AMD after Micron's strong results, and Investor's Business Daily notes the Nasdaq finished at a record as Treasury yields eased from 22-year highs, with the 10-year closing at 5.28 percent.
notes: CNBC original blocked (403); the same weekly story read on Stocktwits, credited. IBD and Bloomberg used for context.
